fatal_errors: The proposed chromium-composition sweep does not reconstruct the AlCoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy coating and post-deposition annealing intervention.
The room-temperature NaCl test omits the governing 3.5 wt.% H2SO4 electrochemical exposure and 900 °C cyclic molten-salt tests.
The numerical baseline, 30% predicted reduction, and 20% falsification threshold are unsupported by the cited evidence.
None of the citations directly tests corrosion as a function of 15–25 wt.% chromium under the proposed conditions.
explanation: The answer offers a testable but conventional chromium-passivation hypothesis. Its Cr-rich passive-film mechanism has limited conceptual overlap with the target, which includes Cr- and Al-rich protective products, but it misses the essential APS AlCoCrFeNi coating, 550 °C annealing optimum, refined microstructure, BCC/FCC phases, sluggish diffusion, and pore-mediated molten-salt degradation. The study has a baseline and falsification rule, yet alloy preparation, compositional controls, replicate strategy, electrochemical measurements, and film-composition analysis are underdeveloped. E2 and E3 support the broad possibility that high-entropy alloys or coatings can resist corrosion, while E1 primarily concerns irradiation tolerance; none validates the proposed chromium sweep or its quantitative claims. Thus it is scientifically plausible in general but insufficiently evidenced and not a reconstruction of the target study.
